newsitem.title: USA: Irwin Q1 helped by home equity business.
newsitem.headline: Irwin Q1 helped by home equity business.

text.p: Irwin Financial Corp said Wednesday a rise in its first quarter earnings and revenues from a year ago reflected improvements at its home equity subsidiary, which offset a decline in mortage banking activities.
Irwin reported net income of $0.45 a share, up from $0.43 a year ag. Total net revenues during the quarter were $52.0 million, up from $44.3 million.

Net income for mortgage banking was $3.9 million in the quarter, a decrease of $1.4 million or 26 percent from a year ago. Mortgage banking results were hurt by rising mortgage loan rates during the quarter, Irwin said.
Mortgage loan originations of $1.1 billion declined $149.0 million or 11.9 percent compared with the 1996 period.
Net income from community banking was $1.4 million in the first quarter, up 7.7 percent from $1.3 million a year earlier.

The home equity lending business earned $1.2 million pre-tax during the first quarter, compared with a pre-tax loss of $2.0 million. This increase reflects revenues associated with the securitization of $60.1 million of home equity loans, Irwin said.
